paper.title_en: An Empirically Calibrated [C II] Luminosity-Halo Mass Relation for Line Intensity Mapping
paper.abstract_en: Millimeter-wave line intensity mapping (LIM) aims to observe the high-redshift universe through the 158 $μ$m fine-structure line of [C II], the brightest far-infrared line of star-forming galaxies. Whether the clustering of large-scale structure, which carries rich cosmological information, is measurable in the [C II] signal at $z>4$ or buried under the shot noise of the emitters is determined from the amplitude and shape of the [C II] power spectrum. We calibrate $L(M_h,z)$ on [C II] data alone: the mean [C II] intensity from tomographic cross-correlation at $0<z<4.2$ and the luminosity-function measurements and limits at $z\simeq0$ and $4.3\lesssim z\lesssim8$. We model the relation as a double power law and fit its four parameters at $z=4.5$ and 5.5 separately, with no assumption about their evolution, and then jointly across $0<z<7$, and we examine how the uncertainty depends on the modeling assumptions. The shape of the power spectrum is settled by the existing data. The clustering peak stands a factor of $45\,(23-93)$ and $64\,(38-112)$ above the shot-noise floor at $z=4.5$ and 5.5, and the two cross at $k_c\simeq 0.37$ and 0.44 $h$ Mpc$^{-1}$. The amplitude is known less well, the clustering power to $0.5-0.6$ dex and the shot noise to $0.7-0.9$ dex. The luminosity-weighted bias, which together with the mean intensity sets the clustering amplitude, is known to about 10\% within the assumptions of this work and is relatively high, about 4. The results show that the signal comes from halos of $10^{11}-10^{12}\,M_\odot$, similar in mass to the hosts of the Lyman-break galaxies and Ly$α$ emitters that galaxy surveys map at these redshifts.
